red_streak_followup: RESOLVED and CONFIRMED. Builder root-caused it: a BoxGeometry has 6 material groups and a single mapped material painted the livery art on ALL faces, including the 0.8 mm side edges where the red logo region showed as a stretched strip (my 'slab side edge catching the texture' hypothesis, confirmed by his mesh inspection: 1 material over 6 groups on both slabs). Fix: a 6-material array with the map only on group 4 (+z front); the other five faces take the housing material — physically correct, since a silkscreen print carries no cut label edge. Added verifyNoWrapAroundTextures() (build fails if a mapped material lands on a multi-group geometry). The fix cascaded into 3 of his own latent defects, each surfaced only when the layer above was made strict: (1) livery_red declared-but-not-rendered after the logo block became art (spec now carries realised_as); (2) his material sweep had ALREADY printed 'declared but not rendered: livery_red' yet exited 0 because that line was a console.log, not an assertion — now it fails; (3) turning the assertion on false-positived livery_print because the sweep read o.material.name (undefined for the new material ARRAYS) — fixed to iterate arrays. Orchestrator re-capture (surface-attempt1-fixed.png, dpr4): the red band that measured 284 saturated-red pixels now measures 0, while the Allen-Bradley logo control region is intact at 22135 red pixels. Streak gone, intended red preserved, console clean.
